question.problem:
A curve is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x={t}^{3}-6{t}^{2}+12t,\,y=4{t}^{2}-3t,\,-\infty <t<\infty .
$$

Determine the value of $t$ at which the tangent to the curve is vertical. Do not round the answer.

The tangent to the curve is vertical at $t=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The slope $m$ of a tangent line to a curve defined parametrically is given by

$$
m=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

The tangent line is vertical if ${x}^{′}(t)=0$ while ${y}^{′}(t)\ne 0.$

So, we first find the derivatives of $x$ and $y:$

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=3{t}^{2}-12t+12,\,{y}^{′}(t)=8t-3
$$

Solving ${x}^{′}(t)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2}-12t+12 & =0 \\ 3({t}^{2}-4t+4) & =0 \\ 3{(t-2)}^{2} & =0\,⟹\,t=2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we note that:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(2) & =8(2)-3\ne 0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the tangent to the curve is vertical at $t=2.$
